subject: science
title: 14.15.2–14.16 Heart Beat, 0.8 s Cardiac Cycle, Heart Sounds & Blood Pressure
subtitle: SA node pacemaker, Bundle of His, Purkinje fibres, LUBB/DUPP sounds, stethoscope & 120/80 mm Hg sphygmomanometer (pp. 209–211)
curiosity_hook: What starts each heartbeat inside your chest without waiting for a brain signal, and which closing valves create the 'LUBB–DUPP' rhythm a doctor hears?
source_verified_by: AGY Pass 2 Full-Chapter Build (pending human biology teacher sign-off)
learning_objectives: Trace myogenic impulse conduction in the human heart: SA Node (pacemaker) → Atria → AV Node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibres → Ventricles.
Break down one 0.8-second Cardiac Cycle into Atrial Systole (0.1 s), Ventricular Systole (0.3 s), and Ventricular Diastole (0.4 s).
Match LUBB (AV valves closing) and DUPP (semilunar valves closing) to stethoscope diagnostics and interpret resting blood pressure (120 / 80 mm Hg).

concept_outline.heading: Myogenic Heartbeat & Pacemaker Conduction (14.15.2, p. 209)
concept_outline.summary: Human heartbeat is myogenic (72–75 beats/min), initiated by the Sino-Atrial (SA) node ('pacemaker') in the right atrial wall near the superior vena cava. The wave spreads over both atria → AV node → Bundle of His (discovered by His, 1893) → Purkinje fibres → ventricular walls.

concept_outline.heading: 0.8 s Cardiac Cycle & LUBB–DUPP Heart Sounds (14.15.3–14.15.4, p. 210)
concept_outline.summary: One cycle (0.8 s) comprises Atrial systole (0.1 s) + Ventricular systole (0.3 s) + Ventricular diastole (0.4 s). First sound LUBB (longer) comes from tricuspid & bicuspid valves closing at the start of ventricular systole; second sound DUPP (shorter) comes from semilunar valves closing at the end of ventricular systole.

concept_outline.heading: Blood Pressure, Stethoscope & Sphygmomanometer (14.16, pp. 210–211)
concept_outline.summary: Normal adult resting BP is 120 mm Hg (systolic) / 80 mm Hg (diastolic), measured on the brachial artery with a sphygmomanometer. Prolonged high BP is hypertension; low BP is hypotension.

key_terms.definition: Specialized cardiac muscle fibres in the right atrium that act as the natural pacemaker of the heart.
Atrial systole (0.1 s) + Ventricular systole (0.3 s) + Ventricular diastole (0.4 s).
LUBB = closure of tricuspid & bicuspid valves; DUPP = closure of pulmonary & aortic semilunar valves.
Clinical instrument measuring brachial-artery systolic/diastolic blood pressure (normal 120/80 mm Hg).

accessible_equivalent.summary: Ordered 0.8-second cardiac cycle breakdown, pacemaker pathway, and BP instrument definitions.

steps.heading: 0.0–0.1 s: Atrial Systole
steps.description: SA node fires; atria contract pushing blood through open tricuspid/bicuspid valves into ventricles.

steps.heading: 0.1–0.4 s: Ventricular Systole (LUBB)
steps.description: AV valves snap shut producing 'LUBB'; ventricles contract ejecting blood through semilunar valves.
steps.key_takeaway: Duration = 0.3 s; generates systolic peak (~120 mm Hg).

steps.heading: 0.4–0.8 s: Ventricular Diastole (DUPP)
steps.description: Semilunar valves snap shut producing 'DUPP'; ventricles relax and refill passively.
steps.key_takeaway: Duration = 0.4 s; diastolic pressure ~80 mm Hg.

question_bank.prompt: Why is the Sino-Atrial (SA) node called the 'pacemaker of the heart' (p. 209)?
question_bank.hint: Remember the human heart is myogenic.

options.label: It spontaneously initiates the electrical impulse that stimulates cardiac muscle contraction
options.feedback: Correct! Located in the right atrium near the superior vena cava, the SA node initiates each beat.

options.label: It pumps blood directly into the aorta
options.feedback: The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta.

options.label: It measures brachial artery blood pressure

question_bank.worked_explanation: The SA node initiates impulses that spread via atria → AV node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibres.

question_bank.prompt: What causes the first heart sound 'LUBB' and the second heart sound 'DUPP' (p. 210)?
question_bank.hint: Match longer LUBB with AV valves and shorter DUPP with semilunar valves.

options.label: LUBB = closure of tricuspid & bicuspid valves; DUPP = closure of semilunar valves
options.feedback: Correct! Valve closure produces both heart sounds heard through a stethoscope.

options.label: LUBB = opening of aorta; DUPP = closing of vena cava
options.feedback: Heart sounds come from valve closure, not opening.

options.label: LUBB = closure of semilunar valves; DUPP = closure of AV valves
options.feedback: Reversed! LUBB happens first (AV valves), DUPP happens second (semilunar valves).

options.label: Both are caused by lung breathing
options.feedback: LUBB and DUPP are purely cardiac valve sounds.

question_bank.worked_explanation: Closure of tricuspid/bicuspid valves at start of ventricular systole makes LUBB; closure of semilunar valves at its end makes DUPP.

question_bank.prompt: What is the total duration of one cardiac cycle and the normal resting adult blood pressure (p. 210)?

options.label: 0.8 second; 120 / 80 mm Hg
options.feedback: Correct! 0.1 + 0.3 + 0.4 = 0.8 s per beat, and normal resting BP is 120/80 mm Hg.

options.label: 1.5 seconds; 80 / 120 mm Hg
options.feedback: Systolic (120) is higher than diastolic (80), and one beat lasts 0.8 s.

options.label: 0.4 second; 160 / 100 mm Hg
options.feedback: 0.4 s is only ventricular diastole; 160/100 is elevated pressure.

options.label: 2.0 seconds; 100 / 60 mm Hg
options.feedback: Check p. 210: 0.8 s cycle and 120 / 80 mm Hg resting BP.

question_bank.worked_explanation: One cardiac cycle lasts 0.8 s (75 beats/min), and healthy resting BP is 120 mm / 80 mm Hg.

worked_feedback: Remember the conduction acronym: SA → AV → His → Purkinje.

flashcards.back: SA Node (pacemaker) → Atria → AV Node → Bundle of His → Purkinje fibres → Ventricles.
Atrial systole (0.1 s) + Ventricular systole (0.3 s) + Ventricular diastole (0.4 s).
Stethoscope detects internal organ/heart sounds (LUBB–DUPP); Sphygmomanometer measures brachial artery blood pressure.
